pages.message: Decline the $11.40 offer; re-engage at $10.50 to $11.30

exhibits.reader_must_see: First Niagara against KeyBank and the peer median on the six metrics the argument rests on
exhibits.comparison: the target against the buyer and against the peer median, metric by metric
exhibits.data: six metrics by three entities, mixed units (multiples, percents, one range)

forms_considered.reason: six metrics in four units would need six scales; the reader reads values, not lengths
chosen: the reader looks values up across a row, and mixed units sit in one grid

forms_considered.form: labelled rows of finding boxes, as the house's slide 10
forms_considered.reason: the house uses them for two estimates side by side; three columns of figures read better as a table

exhibits.why: an executive summary is read for its figures; a table lets each metric be read across the three entities at once

nearest_house_exhibit.what: two estimates side by side by metric in labelled rows; this keeps the side-by-side reading and writes it as a table

exhibits.marks: nothing on the table: the recommendation band under it carries the claim, so the figures stay plain

pages.message: 1.33x tangible book is below the 1.58x precedent median

exhibits.reader_must_see: every precedent's terms, so the median is checkable
exhibits.comparison: nine precedent deals against each other and against the median row
exhibits.data: nine deals by six terms, with a median row

forms_considered.form: comps table with a median row
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the house's slide 5 sets precedents this way and the reader looks terms up
six charts would split a lookup across the page

exhibits.chosen_form: comps table with a median row
exhibits.why: a banker checks the median against the deals it summarises; a table holds both

nearest_house_exhibit.what: a comps table with statistic rows under it; this keeps the median row and drops the max and quartile rows

exhibits.marks: the median row bold with a rule above it, where the comparison is anchored

exhibits.reader_must_see: where 1.33x tangible book falls in the ranking of precedents
exhibits.comparison: the offer's multiple against each precedent's multiple, ranked
exhibits.data: one value for each of nine deals, one of them the subject

forms_considered.form: sorted horizontal bars with the subject in the emphasis colour
forms_considered.reason: chosen: rank and the subject's place read at a glance and the names fit on the left
names would collide where multiples cluster near 1.6x
nine deal names under columns would wrap or turn

exhibits.chosen_form: sorted horizontal bars with the subject in the emphasis colour
exhibits.why: the claim is a rank; sorted bars show the rank, and one dark bar shows where the offer sits

nearest_house_exhibit.what: sorted horizontal bars of synergy run rates with the average boxed; this keeps the sort and marks the subject instead of the average

exhibits.marks: the First Niagara bar in the house's dark fill with its value bold; the other bars muted, values at the bar ends

exhibits.reader_must_see: that the offer line falls to the right of every standalone range's middle
exhibits.comparison: each valuation method's range against the one offer price
exhibits.data: seven low and high pairs in dollars per share, and one offer value

forms_considered.form: floating range bars on one dollar axis with the offer as a vertical line
forms_considered.reason: chosen: every range and the offer share one scale, so above or below reads directly

forms_considered.form: table of lows, highs and midpoints
forms_considered.reason: the reader would subtract to see where the offer falls
loses the width of each range, which is the argument for re-engaging lower

exhibits.chosen_form: floating range bars on one dollar axis with the offer as a vertical line
exhibits.why: the message is a position against a line; ranges on one axis with the line drawn show it without arithmetic

nearest_house_exhibit.none: the reference has no valuation range exhibit; its DDM output on slide 4 is a sensitivity grid of single values, so the ranges are drawn in its navy and its axis text

exhibits.marks: the offer as a labelled vertical line through every bar, where the claim lives

pages.intent: what the price needs from synergies

exhibits.reader_must_see: the gap between precedented and required synergies in each year
exhibits.comparison: precedented synergies against the amount the price requires, by year
exhibits.data: two amounts for each of three years, the second stacked on the first

forms_considered.form: stacked columns, precedented below and the gap above
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the column height is the requirement and the dark top is the gap

forms_considered.form: clustered columns of precedented and required
forms_considered.reason: the gap would be a difference the reader computes between two bars
one bridge shows one year; the gap changes over three years

exhibits.chosen_form: stacked columns, precedented below and the gap above
exhibits.why: the claim is a shortfall each year; the stacked gap is the shortfall drawn

nearest_house_exhibit.what: clustered columns of offer against implied price with the full-synergy columns boxed; this stacks instead, because the gap is the point

exhibits.marks: values inside each segment; the gap in the house's dark fill, nothing else marked

exhibits.reader_must_see: which levers make up the precedented total and how far it falls short
exhibits.comparison: each synergy lever's run-rate against the required total
exhibits.data: four levers by two measures, a total row and a required row

forms_considered.form: table with total and required rows shaded
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the reader looks up each lever and the two totals sit together
the percent of non-interest expense would be a second scale

exhibits.chosen_form: table with total and required rows shaded
exhibits.why: the levers are a build-up to be checked; a table lets the totals be read against each other

nearest_house_exhibit.what: labelled rows of assumptions with values beside them; this writes the same build-up as a table with totals

exhibits.marks: the precedented and required rows shaded and bold, where the shortfall is read
